column7: The remaining half of #2424: a restore that crashed between installing its key files could leave a complete-looking set with one file restored and the others old, which booted and failed at the first decrypt. #3583's restore journal makes the server refuse while it exists and --recover finish or undo the install; the key-set manifest that records the restored set is now one more entry of that journal, installed after the key files (prepareRestoredKeySet), so with the journal present boot and every key writer name --recover, and without it (journal lost) the manifest check still refuses the half-installed set as not matching the recorded hashes, naming the file. The test kills a real restore process after it installed dek.key, on SQLite (default-ci) and PostgreSQL (when KEYORIX_TEST_PG_DSN is set), and checks both refusals and the roll-forward. Also TestAdminRestore_Overwrite_KillPoints (manifest byte-identical before the commit point, recording the archive's keys after recovery) and server:TestVerifyKeyFileSetConsistency_JournalRefusalComesBeforeManifestMismatch.
